issues.legal_issue: A statutory abolition of hereditary land tenure and its incidents does not, without more, make an existing decree for possession of the land unenforceable where the former holder retains a statutory right to possession under a regrant scheme.
material_facts: A decree for possession of the land had been obtained by a hereditary office-holder against persons occupying it.
A later enactment abolished the hereditary tenure and extinguished its incidents, but provided for the land to be regranted to the former holder subject to conditions.
The enactment did not expressly provide that existing possession decrees would become unenforceable.
issues.conclusion: The decree remained executable, subject to the former holder's entitlement to possession under the statutory regrant scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4, abolition of the tenure and extinguishment of its incidents were subject to sections 6, 7 and 10. Section 6 provided for regrant to the former holder, who would be deemed an occupant and could retain possession on compliance with its conditions; section 7 made provision for authorised holders, while section 10 provided for eviction of unauthorised holders. Because the enactment contained no provision making existing possession decrees unenforceable, the former holder's right to execute the decree was not extinguished. The Court distinguished Chhote Khan v. Mohammad Obedulla Khan, AIR 1953 Nag. 361, because the legislation considered there lacked corresponding regrant provisions, and expressed no view on the correctness of that decision.

rule.if: execution_of_existing_possession_decree and decree_awarded_to_former_tenure_holder and holder_retains_conditional_possession_right and not express_bar_to_decree_execution

predicates.execution_of_existing_possession_decree: A party sought to enforce an existing decree awarding possession of land.
predicates.decree_awarded_to_former_tenure_holder: The possession decree had been awarded to a person who held the land under the former hereditary tenure.
predicates.holder_retains_conditional_possession_ri: The later legal scheme allowed the former holder to retain possession of the land upon satisfying prescribed conditions.
predicates.express_bar_to_decree_execution: The later legal scheme expressly made existing possession decrees unenforceable.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to enforce a possession decree awarded to a former tenure-holder, the decree remains executable if the holder retains a conditional right to possession and the later legal scheme does not expressly bar its execution.

issues.legal_issue: A clause making an abolition enactment effective notwithstanding decrees or court orders does not, by mentioning those decrees or orders, itself prohibit execution of an existing possession decree.
material_facts: The enactment's opening clause referred to decrees and orders of a court alongside settlements, grants, agreements and similar instruments.
The clause provided that the enactment's specified effects would apply notwithstanding those instruments.
The proceeding concerned execution of a possession decree obtained before the enactment took effect.
issues.conclusion: The reference to decrees and orders did not make the possession decree unexecutable; it ensured that the enactment's specified effects applied despite instruments that defined or declared incidents of the former tenure.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the ejusdem generis principle, as stated in Maxwell on the Interpretation of Statutes, 12th edition, page 297: general words following particular words ordinarily refer to things of the same kind as those specifically listed. Read in context, the phrase covering decrees and court orders meant that they could not prevent the specified statutory changes to the tenure and its incidents; it did not prohibit execution of a possession decree.

predicates.execution_of_existing_possession_decree: A party sought to enforce an existing decree awarding possession of land.
predicates.decree_listed_with_settlements_and_grant: The enactment referred to court decrees alongside settlements, grants and similar instruments.
predicates.clause_makes_statutory_changes_effective: The enactment stated that its specified changes applied notwithstanding the listed instruments.

issues.definition: In an execution proceeding, a reference to court decrees alongside settlements and grants does not bar execution when the clause uses that list to make specified statutory changes effective despite those instruments.
